title: Ukraine exposes ransomware network extorting US oil, healthcare firms
content_md: Ukrainian authorities arrested four suspected members of an international ransomware network accused of extorting more than $40 million from companies around the world. The operation, carried out in cooperation with the FBI, targeted a criminal organization with at least 27 members from countries including Ukraine, Russia and Kazakhstan, Ukraine's Prosecutor General's Office said Wednesday. Authorities linked the group, which they did not name, to a wider network of more than 60 people operating across eight jurisdictions, including former members of the notorious Conti ransomware gang. The hackers extorted at least 28 companies for a combined $40.5 million, although authorities said the total financial damage could be higher. The hackers targeted companies in the oil and gas, pharmaceutical, manufacturing and logistics industries, as well as financial institutions and critical infrastructure operators. During the international law enforcement operation, Ukrainian police conducted 66 coordinated searches in Kyiv and 11 other regions of the country, reportedly with the participation of U.S. law enforcement officials. Investigators seized computers, mobile phones, bank cards, about $370,000 in cash and 20,000 euros (nearly $22,000). The four suspected key members of the organization could face up to 15 years in prison if convicted. Authorities said they were continuing to identify other members of the network.
